title: POC Weekly - Redwood Private VPC Pilot Sync
summary: Weekly sync for the Redwood Private VPC pilot. Covered recent networking flaps, routing configuration fixes, a brief review of benchmark results (latency and throughput), a plan for runtime upgrade, and security questions about audit logs and KMS. Agreed next steps: share updated network diagram, run a targeted 10k-token benchmark, SE to test a kernel-config tweak, and schedule a security follow-up with the customer GRC team.
next_steps: Maya to share updated VPC networking diagram and route tables by 2026-08-03
Carlos to run 10k-token throughput benchmark and share raw CSV by 2026-08-05
Sofia to coordinate GRC meeting with Redwood security team the week of 2026-08-10
Tom to validate peering after route change and confirm connectivity by 2026-08-02
action_items: Maya Chen - Send updated network diagram and notes (due 2026-08-03)
Carlos Duarte - Run kernel-config benchmark (10k-token, heavy context) and upload results (due 2026-08-05)
Sofia Gomez - Arrange GRC/security follow-up w/ Redwood (target week of 2026-08-10)
Tom Reynolds - Re-run connectivity tests and confirm VPC routes after change (due 2026-08-02)
Aisha Patel - Provide production inference sample set for quality checks (due 2026-08-06)
header:
Date: 2026-07-29
Time: 10:00 AM - 10:45 AM UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Duarte (Redwood SE), Ivy Park (Redwood CSM), Aisha Patel (Northpoint Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (Infra), Sofia Gomez (Security), Liam O'Connor (DevOps)
transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll keep this to 45 minutes. Quick roll call?
00:08 Aisha Patel: Hi, Aisha here.
00:10 Tom Reynolds: Tom, on infra.
00:12 Sofia Gomez: Sofia, security.
00:14 Liam O'Connor: Liam, DevOps.
00:16 Carlos Duarte: Carlos from Redwood engineering.
00:18 Ivy Park: Ivy, CSM.
00:20 Maya Chen: Cool. Quick agenda \u0014 networking update, bench results, planned upgrade to the private control plane, and outstanding security items. Start with network, Tom?
00:37 Tom Reynolds: Yeah so we hit that intermittent routing flap on Friday after the route table change. We saw some packets getting blackholed between the prod-subnet and the dedicated subnet for the pilot. We rolled back the change and things came back. We tried the route update in staging and it looked fine, but prod had a slightly different set of peering rules.
00:58 Maya Chen: Right. We traced it to a missing propagate on the route table \u0014 the terraform module didn't tag one of the route propagations, so the control-plane couldn't reach one of the worker subnets for the gRPC calls.
01:12 Carlos Duarte: Yep, that was the symptom. When the control-plane couldn't reach the workers we saw the keepalive failovers and the fallback to hosted endpoints for a small percentage of requests. That explains the latency spikes you observed.
01:28 Aisha Patel: When it failed over to hosted, did any data leave our VPC? We're very sensitive about egress.
01:35 Maya Chen: The failover is to Redwood-verified hosted model variants in our infra \u0014 we do not retain customer data in logs for those calls, but I know you asked about strict egress. We can adjust the policy to not failover for the pilot while we sort the routing, or keep the failover disabled.
01:51 Sofia Gomez: For compliance, we want absolute no-eject for our pilot. So please keep automatic fallback off until we finish the audit.
01:58 Maya Chen: Understood. We'll turn automatic fallback off and we'll keep a manual escalation path.
02:05 Tom Reynolds: I'll reapply the corrected propagate flag and run the peering validation script. I'll report back after reattach.
02:12 Maya Chen: Great, add that as an action. Carlos, quick on the bench \u0014 any changes this week?
02:20 Carlos Duarte: Yeah, we ran the 5k-token baseline again with the new batching config. Summary \u0014 median p50 latency dropped about 8% on nv4 instances, throughput increased by ~12% when we enabled the adaptive KV cache. However, in the long-tail we still see occasional 500\u0013700 ms spikes at scale, looks correlated with KV cache misses and cold model loads during long-context traces.
02:46 Aisha Patel: Are those spikes reproducible on our dataset?
02:49 Carlos Duarte: We saw them in two of the target traces you sent, specifically the dialogs with ~8k context. We haven't run the full 10k yet \u0014 that's next. The adaptive cache reduces average token cost but the cache warm-up pattern needs more tuning.
03:04 Maya Chen: We had suggested a configuration tweak to kernel selection for long sequences \u0014 did you test that?
03:09 Carlos Duarte: I did a small run. Switching to the fused-attention kernel for sequences > 4k helps but it also increases GPU memory usage by about 6\u00138%. On our test instance that was okay, but for your environment we need to check memory headroom.
03:24 Liam O'Connor: Memory headroom is tight on the current instance family, we picked it to save costs. If fused kernels need more headroom that's a tradeoff \u0014 do we scale instance size or push more quantization?
03:36 Carlos Duarte: We can also try 4-bit quantization for the KV cache path which reduces footprint and keeps latency reasonable. There's a small quality delta but it may be acceptable for some routes.
03:47 Aisha Patel: Quality delta \u0014 we need a clear metric. We'll provide a holdout set, can you run the quantized run and compare perplexity and top-1 on our evals?
03:58 Maya Chen: Yes \u0014 that's on the action list: Aisha will send the eval set, Carlos will run quantized and non-quantized 10k-token runs and share the CSVs.
04:07 Ivy Park: Quick note \u0014 I uploaded the deck with the kernel-config options to the shared drive (link in chat).
04:15 Sofia Gomez: On security questions \u0014 we reviewed audit logs last week. Two things: we need confirmation that control plane audit logs are delivered to our central SIEM with the same retention as app logs, and we need validation that KMS keys are customer-managed.
04:31 Maya Chen: For this pilot, the Private control plane can be configured with customer KMS via our KMS integration \u0014 that's supported. For audit logs, we have a forwarder that ships control-plane events to your S3 bucket or to a Syslog endpoint; retention is configurable.
04:45 Sofia Gomez: Can you provide the schema for the audit events? Field names, timestamps, and the user field mappings? Last time the event names were slightly different and we had to map them in the SIEM.
04:56 Carlos Duarte: We'll export the event schema. There may be slight naming differences \u0014 Redwood internal names may appear, I can add a mapping table to make ingestion deterministic.
05:08 Aisha Patel: Also, SLA question \u0014 if we disable automatic fallback per Sofia's ask, what SLA impact does that have?
05:15 Maya Chen: Disabling automated failover means the pilot stays within the VPC; if the control plane can't reach workers requests will fail rather than be served by hosted fallbacks. We can set up active alerting and a manual runbook to flip on emergency routing, but SLA terms for Dedicated/Private pilot are discussed in the contract \u0014 we'll include that in the security follow-up.
05:36 Liam O'Connor: Another networking item \u0014 cross-region routing. Our DR plan has some subnets in eu-west-1 and the pilot sits primary in us-east-1. If we need cross-region fallback we'll want to verify latency and egress compliance.
05:51 Maya Chen: Noted \u0014 we'll add cross-region tests to the benchmark.
05:55 Tom Reynolds: Ok, I re-ran the peering validator with the corrected propagate and it now shows full connectivity, I'll watch the metric for the next 24 hours.
06:05 Carlos Duarte: On the upgrade side \u0014 Redwood plans a minor control-plane release on 2026-08-06 with improved KV cache eviction heuristics. The upgrade is backward compatible but we'll want to schedule it in a maintenance window since it restarts a couple of control-plane pods.
06:21 Aisha Patel: Any risk to in-flight requests?
06:23 Carlos Duarte: We drain existing sessions, but very long-running streaming calls may be aborted; best to schedule a low-traffic window.
06:31 Maya Chen: Proposal \u0014 schedule upgrade for 2026-08-07 02:00 UTC, notify you 48 hours in advance, and provide rollback plan. Thoughts?
06:40 Sofia Gomez: Works for us pending GRC signoff.
06:43 Aisha Patel: Agree.
06:45 Ivy Park: I'll send calendar hold after this call.
06:48 Maya Chen: Anything else?
06:50 Liam O'Connor: Two quick asks \u0014 can Carlos share the exact kernel flags you changed and the experimental conf? Also, can we get the raw bench CSVs with timestamps?
06:59 Carlos Duarte: Yes, I'll upload the raw CSVs and the kernel-config diff to the shared folder.
07:05 Tom Reynolds: Also, can you add the exact route table change you made? We want the Terraform diff to mirror prod fix.
07:12 Maya Chen: I'll attach the terraform diff and the updated route table diagram.
07:16 Aisha Patel: One last thing \u0014 on quality regression monitoring, can Redwood tie eval alerts to a Slack channel and paging if top-line metrics drop?
07:25 Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Optimize can emit alerts to Slack or PagerDuty on eval regressions \u0014 we'll enable a pilot integration. We'll need the threshold rules from you.
07:35 Aisha Patel: We'll send thresholds with the eval set.
07:39 Maya Chen: Great. Recap: turn off automatic fallback, Tom will validate routes, Maya will send network diagram and terraform diff, Carlos will run the 10k-token benchmarks including quantized runs and share CSVs, Sofia to set up GRC meeting. We'll schedule control-plane upgrade for 2026-08-07 pending signoff.
07:59 Ivy Park: I'll capture action items in the ticket and follow up.
08:03 Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, next sync same time next week unless we need a mid-week GRC loop.
08:09 Aisha Patel: Thanks all.
08:11 Meeting end.
